summary: Service providers publish a signed baseline from their own cloud, with no management server and no expiring links to renew.

new.title: Baseline published from the provider's cloud
new.text: A scheduled job in the managing tenant's Azure builds and signs the baseline with a key that never leaves its key vault. No management server is needed.

new.title: Deploy as a signed-in administrator
new.text: The one-command build can now run on your own sign-in instead of a certificate-based deployment identity.

new.title: Private-only deployments supported
new.text: The managing tenant and each managed tenant can run with no public entry point, reading the baseline through a private connection.

fixes.title: Managed tenants trust only the pinned key
fixes.text: Each managed tenant accepts a baseline only from the provider key it is set up with. Several keys can be pinned, so keys change without a gap.
fixes.action: Update every managed tenant and pin the provider's key before the provider's first cloud publish, and redeploy the baseline jobs with this version.

fixes.title: No expiring read link any more
fixes.text: Managed tenants read the signed baseline over the network, so nothing in the access path expires or needs renewing.

fixes.title: Smaller fixes
fixes.text: The one-command build completes on a new pair, the Manager says why a baseline is not verified, and a check without directory rights reports not checked.
fixes.action: Before building a brand-new pair, do the two preparation steps listed in the build guide.
